assessments.reasoning: The XPath 3.1 array definition assigns positive integer keys to member positions and fixes the first position at 1. The additional constructor passage establishes the counting unit: an argument whose value is a sequence supplies one member, including when that sequence is empty.

challenge.method: Distinguish an empty array from an array whose first member is an empty sequence. Check whether a subsequent multi-item member occupies several positions.
challenge.results: An empty array has no first member. The example with an empty sequence followed by a three-item sequence has two members. The empty sequence occupies position 1 and the entire subsequent sequence occupies position 2.

limitations: An array member can be a sequence. Positions count members, not their contained items.
The rule concerns positions in XPath arrays. Sequence items within a member do not renumber the members.
